sections.label: Work injury compensation claims payouts
sections.summary: Over three years, about 15,000 work injury compensation claims were awarded yearly, with payouts near $115 million per year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Over the past three years, an average of about 15,000 work injury compensation claims were awarded, with a total payout close to $115 million per year for wage and lump-sum compensation.

sections.label: New Work Injury Compensation Act 2019
sections.summary: WICA will be repealed and replaced by a new Act, the Work Injury Compensation Act 2019, giving employers greater assurance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Fourth, we will give greater assurance to employers so that WICA provides a balanced package of safeguards for both employers and injured employees.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: So, the existing WICA will be repealed and replaced by a new Act, the Work Injury Compensation Act 2019.

sections.label: Insurers sharing policy and claims information
sections.summary: Clause 33 of the Bill will require insurers to share policy and claims information with the Commissioner.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Clause 33 of the Bill will require insurers to share policy and claims information with the Commissioner.

sections.label: Insurer checks delay claim processing
sections.summary: Under the current system, insurers checking claim details with employers, workers and MOM can delay processing by up to six weeks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Under the current system, having the insurers check back with the employers, the workers and with MOM on the claim details can delay processing by up to six weeks.

sections.label: Fixed formula for compensation amount
sections.summary: Insurers have no discretion in determining compensation, which is a fixed formula based on incapacity, working life and average monthly earnings.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Second, insurers do not have discretion in determining the compensation amount as it is a fixed formula based on three factors: one, the doctor's assessment of the extent of incapacity; two, the worker’s remaining years of working life; and three, the worker's average monthly earnings (AME).

sections.label: PI claims resolved within six months
sections.summary: Today, about 80% of PI claims every year are resolved within six months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Today, about 80% of PI claims every year are resolved within six months.

sections.label: AME disputes received yearly
sections.summary: The Ministry receives about 360 AME disputes a year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: The Ministry receives about 360 AME disputes a year.

sections.label: Clause 35 claim deemed made
sections.summary: Clause 35 provides a claim is deemed made when the employer first receives notice of the accident, to speed processing and reduce employees being misled or ignorant of procedures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: To speed up claims processing and reduce the risk of employees being misled or being ignorant of application procedures, clause 35 of the Bill provides that a claim is deemed to be made when the employer first receives notice of the accident.

sections.label: Phase 1 compulsory insurance expansion
sections.summary: Phase 1 extends compulsory insurance to non-manual employees earning up to $2,100 a month regardless of workplace, planned for 2020 and 2021, covering around 300,000 more employees.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: In Phase 1, we will extend compulsory insurance to non-manual employees earning up to $2,100 a month, regardless of where they work, and we plan to do this in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: And we plan to do this in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: This expansion will require around 300,000 more employees to be covered by the compulsory insurance requirement.

sections.label: Increased compensation limits
sections.summary: Death and PI compensation limits rise about 10% to $225,000 and $289,000, and medical expenses rise from $36,000 to $45,000, about 25%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: The compensation limits for death and PI will increase by about 10% to $225,000 and $289,000 respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: The compensation limit for medical expenses will be raised from the current $36,000 to $45,000, an increase of about 25%.

sections.label: Clause 30 unapproved insurer offence
sections.summary: Clause 30 makes it an offence for insurers not approved by the Commissioner as a designated insurer to sell a WICA-compliant policy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Additionally, clause 30 makes it an offence for any insurers not approved by the Commissioner as a designated insurer to sell a WICA-compliant policy.

sections.label: Clause 61 penalty increase
sections.summary: Clause 61 increases the maximum fine for non- or late payment of compensation from $10,000 to $15,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: On penalties, clause 61 increases the maximum fine for non- or late payment of compensation from the current $10,000 to $15,000.

sections.label: Doubled fines for repeat offenders
sections.summary: Clauses 25, 35, 61, 62 and 68 double maximum fines for a second or subsequent offence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: To deter repeat offenders, clauses 25, 35, 61, 62 and 68 provide for the maximum fines for a second or subsequent offence to be doubled.

sections.label: WIC Bill effective date
sections.summary: The new WIC Bill, if passed, will be effected on 1 September 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: The new WIC Bill, if passed, will be effected on 1 September 2020.

sections.label: MOM reporting and accreditation
sections.summary: MOM requires reporting of all MCs or light duties from work injuries and will accredit a standard WIC policy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: First, there is now a mandatory requirement by MOM to report all instances of medical certificates (MCs) or light duties due to work injuries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Second, MOM will now accredit a standard WIC policy with a core set of insurance terms and conditions, which reduces disputes from policies with complex policy exclusions.

sections.label: Higher compensation and medical limits
sections.summary: The amendments increase compensation amounts and medical limits in view of rising wages and healthcare costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Third, under the amendments, there will be an increase in the compensation amount and medical limits, in view of rising wages and healthcare costs.

sections.label: Compulsory insurance for non-manual employees
sections.summary: Compulsory insurance coverage expands to non-manual employees in non-factories earning up to S$2,600, benefiting 25,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Lastly, the effect of the amendments is the expansion of compulsory insurance coverage to more non-manual employees (NMEs) working in non-factories earning up to S$2,600, an increase from the current S$1,600, which will benefit another 25,000 workers, which comprise largely of junior professionals, managers and executives (PMEs).

sections.label: Compensation increase and AME limits
sections.summary: The Bill generally increases work injury compensation, but employees get full AME only for the first 14 days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: It is, first, commendable that there is a general increase in the compensation for work injuries under this Bill to keep pace with wage growth and healthcare costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, we note that under the proposed amendments, employees will only be compensated the full average monthly earnings (AME) for the first 14 days of MC and/or light duties, and thereafter, only two-thirds AME of up to one year.

sections.label: Expanding mandatory insurance coverage
sections.summary: Mandatory insurance coverage expands to non-manual employees earning up to $2,600 a month, with compensation levels raised and further expansion proposed gradually in consultation with employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The expansion of mandatory insurance coverage to non-manual employees earning up to $2,600 a month, together with the lifting of compensation levels to keep pace with wage growth and rising medical costs, provides enhanced protection for vulnerable workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: In parallel with this enhancement, efforts must be stepped up to raise workers' awareness of their rights under the WIC framework and to also better monitor employers' compliance with the maintenance of mandatory coverage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Of course, this suggestion may face resistance from employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, to alleviate any such worries, it is proposed that the expansion of mandatory insurance coverage protecting workers earning beyond S$2,600 be imposed gradually, in consultation with employers and in tandem with economic growth over the years.

sections.label: Monitoring employers' insurance compliance
sections.summary: Insurer data sharing lets MOM monitor mandatory coverage for foreign workers, with audits, safety nets for injured workers and possible Workers' Fund contributions from premiums.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: With the sharing of policy and claims data by licensed insurers with MOM and other licensed insurers, MOM can now implement a better monitoring system to ensure that employers maintain mandatory insurance coverage for foreign workers throughout the validity of their work passes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Audits should also be conducted on the insurance policies procured by the employer to ensure that adequate coverage has been secured for their workers and the type of work undertaken by the workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Even with good processes in place, there must also be provision for cases which slip through the cracks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: We must ensure that there are adequate safety nets in place to help injured workers to seek medical treatment and compensation in the event where the employer has failed to perform their obligations under WICA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: With the increase in WIC insurance premiums, it may be timely to explore if a small percentage of the premiums could be channelled to grow the Workers' Fund to provide relief in such exigencies.

sections.label: Non-manual workers coverage threshold
sections.summary: Under the Bill, non-manual workers earning up to $2,600 will be covered in stages, up from the current $1,600.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With the changes proposed under this Bill, non-manual workers receiving a salary of up to $2,600 will also be covered in stages, up from $1,600, as is currently the case.

sections.label: Payout after challenged medical report
sections.summary: After a medical report initially challenged by the insurer, R received a payout of 25% of PI amounting to $54,500.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: After the submission of a medical report which was initially challenged by the insurer, R eventually received a payout of 25% of PI which amounted to $54,500.

sections.label: WICA claims data questions
sections.summary: Citing 2016-2017 figures, it asks for percentages and numbers of successful WICA claims and breakdowns of workers choosing other routes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the former Minister for Manpower in a reply to a Parliamentary Question in January 2018, out of the 33,000-plus WICA claims in the two years from 2016 to 2017, about 2,500 claims were withdrawn either because workers received private compensation from their employers, chose to pursue a common law remedy or decided not to proceed with their claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To give the House a sense of the latest numbers involved, what was the percentage and absolute number of successful WICA claims by foreign and local workers over the last five years and, separately, what is the breakdown of workers who chose a common law remedy, private compensation and did not proceed with their claims respectively?

sections.label: Light duties compensation amendments
sections.summary: The amendments compensate injured workers up to usual earnings on light duties, provide simplified reporting, and shift claim filing responsibility to employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The amendments see that an injured worker will be compensated up to their usual level of earnings if they are given light duties by a doctor, principally because they would not be able to undertake overtime work to boost their wages while on light duties, hence a lower AME calculation for the purposes of their claim.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Ministry has stressed that such reporting will not be an administrative burden for employers and has provided for a simplified procedure for reporting injuries that result in less than four days of light duties or MC for the worker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under the Bill, the responsibility shifts to the employer to file a WICA claim as employees now do not have to separately file a claim.

sections.label: Insurers to process death and PI claims
sections.summary: The amendments make insurers process death and PI claims, a function previously done by MOM.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under the proposed amendments, insurers will now also process death and PI claims, a function that was previously undertaken by MOM.

sections.label: Worker choice of doctor
sections.summary: A question asks whether the Commissioner of Labour would let workers see a doctor of their choice rather than the employer's choice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In one story last year, The Straits Times senior health correspondent, in a story titled, "Doctors reminded to give injured workers the rest they need", noted that the Ministry had reported three doctors to the Medical Council for not ordering the requisite rest or recovery period commensurate with the worker's injury.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, in view of the power imbalance between employer and worker, would the Commissioner of Labour consider giving effect to requests by workers to see a doctor of their choice, possibly one on a panel managed by the Ministry, as opposed to being restricted to choose a doctor of the employer's choice?

sections.label: Payment for second consultation
sections.summary: A question asks who would pay for the second consultation, noting most workers should not face claim difficulties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can I just confirm who would pay for that second consultation?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the main, the majority of workers should not face any difficulties with their claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, laws like WICA that are a critical expression of our social attitudes and shape our social compact – in this case towards manual workers and non-manual workers who earn less than $2,600 – are often judged on where they fall short and the cases which slip through the cracks.

sections.label: Overhaul of work injury compensation regime
sections.summary: The Bill proposes an overhaul of the work injury compensation regime, expanding WICA coverage, licensing WIC insurers, and simplifying claims processes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill proposes an overhaul of the existing work injury compensation regime which, on the whole, benefits both employees and employers by expanding WICA coverage, licensing WIC insurers, and simplifying and expediting work injury claims processes.

sections.label: Criteria for reporting an injury
sections.summary: The criteria for reporting an injury will be at least 24 hours of hospitalisation or any medical leave or light duties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The criteria for reporting an injury will now be at least 24 hours of hospitalisation or any instance of medical leave or light duties.

sections.label: Compensation coverage for light duties
sections.summary: The Bill extends compensation coverage to employees on light duties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Next, the Bill also extends compensation coverage to employees on light duties.

sections.label: Automatic claim application system
sections.summary: The amendments will introduce an automatic claim application system for fatal or serious injuries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The amendments will also introduce an automatic claim application system for fatal or serious injuries.

sections.label: Insurance cards for insured employees
sections.summary: It asks whether the licensing regime for insurers can require insured employees to be issued insurance cards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, can the licensing regime for insurers also include a requirement that insured employees be issued with insurance cards to facilitate faster processing of medical appointments and procedures?

sections.label: Letter for migrant worker claims
sections.summary: It asks whether the Ministry can issue such a letter to a migrant worker without a bank account.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As a matter of standard practice, when commencing a work injury claim, can the Ministry issue such a letter to a migrant worker who does not already have a bank account?

sections.label: Insurers determining AME difficulties
sections.summary: It asks how the Ministry intends to address difficulties insurers may face in determining AME.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share how the Ministry intends to address the possible difficulties that insurers may face in determining AME?

sections.label: Exceptions to one-year time bar
sections.summary: It asks whether exceptions to the one-year time bar can be introduced where employers prevent employees from getting medical treatment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry introduce exceptions to the one-year time bar where the employer has actively sought to prevent the employee from getting medical treatment?

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If we truly wish to provide workers with one of the safest and healthiest workplaces in the world, as recommended by the WSH2028 Tripartite Strategies Committee in April 2019, we must take into account their working realities, especially our 970,000 migrant workers who form the bulk of our manual labour force and, therefore, most at-risk from work injuries.

sections.label: TADM found underpaid wages
sections.summary: TADM found the worker was incorrectly paid before the injury, computing $13,000 underpaid over 12 months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While the WICA case was ongoing, the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM) had found that he was incorrectly paid before the injury and computed the total underpaid amount as $13,000 over 12 months.

sections.label: Migrant workers' insurance coverage survey
sections.summary: A 2016 BMJ Global Health survey of 433 migrant workers in Singapore found only 61.4% were certain they had medical insurance coverage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to the British Medical Journal (BMJ) Global Health Journal, a 2016 survey conducted by medical practitioners with 433 migrant workers in Singapore found that only 61.4% of these workers were certain that they had medical insurance coverage.

sections.label: Ahmad's missed MRI scans
sections.summary: Ahmad, injured at work five months ago, missed two MRI scan appointments because his employer did not pay bills or issue undertakings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Ahmad sustained a severe back injury at work when he fell while carrying heavy construction material five months ago.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: He required magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans for ongoing treatment but had to miss two scan appointments because his employer did not pay outstanding bills nor issue undertakings to pay for ongoing treatment.

sections.label: Insurance cards and 30-day timeline
sections.summary: The speaker proposes insurers issue workers insurance cards acting as a Letter of Guarantee, and recommends a 30-day target to determine work-relatedness.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the meantime, to circumvent the challenge of employers promptly providing the Letter of Guarantee, I propose that workers be issued with insurance cards by the insurer that acts as a Letter of Guarantee, to facilitate easier and faster processing of medical appointments, medical procedures and scans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A 30-day timeline as a target is recommended to determine whether the injury is work-related and, hence, treatment should be covered under insurance.

sections.label: Workers' claims and mental illness survey
sections.summary: A 2015 Singapore Management University survey of 605 Bangladeshi and Indian workers found over 60% with outstanding injury or salary claims predicted to have serious mental illness.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A 2015 survey of 605 Bangladeshi and Indian workers conducted by the Singapore Management University found that more than 60% of respondents who had outstanding injury or salary claims were predicted to have serious mental illness.

sections.label: Permits cancelled after injury
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Minister to let injured workers whose permits employers cancelled prematurely, but who are free from medical leave or light duties, look for new jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Last but not least, I urge the Minister to consider allowing workers who have had their permits cancelled prematurely by employers after they have suffered an injury, but are free from medical leave or light duties, to look for new jobs instead of being sent back home unfairly when they have already recuperated.

sections.label: Work Injury Compensation Act history
sections.summary: The Workmen's Compensation Act was enacted in 1975, renamed WICA in 2008, and reviewed in 2016 with increased compensation limits for death and total permanent incapacity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Workmen’s Compensation Act was first enacted in 1975, an Act related to the payment of compensation to workmen for injury suffered in the course of their employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2008, the Act was reviewed and renamed as the Work Injury Compensation Act (WICA), which aims to provide low-cost and expeditious resolution of work-related injury claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: WICA was last reviewed in 2016 where the maximum and minimum compensation limits for death and total permanent incapacity were increased.

sections.label: Work injury cases and compensation
sections.summary: MOM statistics show 14,585 work injury cases in 2018, with $21.89 million for medical leave wages and $89.84 million for permanent incapacity and death compensation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Yet, according to MOM statistics, there were 14,585 work injury cases in 2018, amounting to $21.89 million in compensation for medical leave wages and $89.84 million for permanent incapacity and death compensation.

sections.label: Insurers sharing data with MOM
sections.summary: Insurers would be required to share policy and claims information with MOM to centralise data and let insurers offer differentiated premiums based on employers' risk profile and claims history.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Insurers would now be required to share policy and claims information with MOM.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The objective of this proposed change is to allow centralisation and sharing of data amongst insurers to allow them to offer insurance plans of differentiated premiums to employers of different risk profile and claims history.

sections.label: Medical inflation and MediShield Life
sections.summary: A recent report expects Singapore's annual medical inflation rate to be 10% this year, and tripartite partners advocate this as it reduces duplication of coverage and arrests rising medical expenses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, and on a separate note, according to a recent report, the annual medical inflation rate for Singapore is expected to be 10% for this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The tripartite partners have been advocating this as it reduces duplication of coverage between the employer's medical benefits and MediShield Life and will also arrest the increase in overall medical expenses.

sections.label: WICA coverage for contractors
sections.summary: WICA coverage is available to workers under a contract of service but not workers for their own accounts, such as delivery riders who are contractors choosing their own work arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: WICA coverage is available to workers employed under a contract of service, but not workers for their own accounts, whatever their occupation or income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, it is widely accepted that many delivery riders are contractors and not employees because they may choose their own work arrangements, such as riding their own vehicles and managing their own working hours.

sections.label: Self-employed persons insurance recommendations
sections.summary: The Tripartite Workgroup on Self Employed Persons notes most self-employed persons work in low-risk desk-bound jobs and recommends promoting private insurance for higher-risk occupations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: How much of a capital investment does an e-scooter for food delivery represent, for example?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Also, Sir, the Tripartite Workgroup on Self Employed Persons notes that the majority of self-employed persons in Singapore work in desk-bound non-manual jobs where the risk of injury is low.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And for the smaller group of self-employed persons engaged in higher-risk occupations, it recommends that the Government promote the adoption of private insurance in higher-risk occupations through licensing controls or tapping on the Government’s role as a service-buyer, where possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Higher injury compensations and broader insurance coverage to more workers give greater insurance to our working people and it is timely with the rising cost of living and medical expenses.

sections.label: Salary threshold for compulsory insurance
sections.summary: The move to expand compulsory insurance coverage to non-manual employees is welcomed, but the proposed salary threshold increase from $1,600 to $2,600 is still low.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While the move to expand compulsory insurance coverage to non-manual employees is welcomed, the salary threshold with proposed amendments from $1,600 to $2,600 is still low.

sections.label: Platform economy self-employed persons
sections.summary: The platform economy has led to a growing number of self-employed persons, estimated at more than 200,000 in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With the advent of the platform economy, we have a growing number of self-employed persons, estimated to be more than 200,000 in Singapore.

sections.label: Work stress mental illness coverage
sections.summary: Mental illness from work stress is increasingly common but is not covered by the WICA amendments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My third point of clarification is on mental illness brought about by work stress which is increasingly common in the workplace but it is not covered by the WICA amendments.

sections.label: HSSE Council union management feedback
sections.summary: The HSSE Council, comprising management and union representatives and chaired by top management, meets regularly to review safety and health performance and address workers' concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As part of this close partnership, there are many channels for union leaders to provide feedback to management, in particular, the Health, Safety, Security Environment (HSSE) Council, which comprises management and union representatives and chaired by the top management executive, is a platform with regular meetings to jointly review safety and health performance, set safety and health directions, and provide feedback to management about workers' concern in safety-related as well as health, security and environment-related issues.

sections.label: PSA safety technologies and programmes
sections.summary: PSA uses video analytics and telematics to improve on-the-job behaviour and prevent accidents, alongside pre-emptive intervention programmes of mentoring, coaching and training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, PSA taps on technologies, such as video analytics and telematics, to improve on-the-job behaviour and prevent accidents to the pre-emptive intervention programmes aimed at mentoring, coaching and training workers to improve their safety behaviour.

sections.label: Labour Movement welcomes amendments, mental illness
sections.summary: The Labour Movement welcomes the amendments benefiting workers and hopes the Ministry will cover every worker, including those with mental illness, under the Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To conclude, Sir, the Labour Movement welcomes these additional amendments that bring benefits to the workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We do hope that the Ministry can look at ways to cover every worker, including workers with mental illness, under the Act.

sections.label: Support for Bill, claims and insurance
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill, which provides faster compensation for work injuries, minimum insurance standards, and full employer insurance coverage, and welcomes claims processing upon notification of fatal or serious injuries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: After all, the well-being of our members is always our core business.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I stand in support of this Bill which will, first, provide for affected employees to receive compensation for work injuries more expeditiously; second, ensure that the insurance policies meet minimum standards; and third, employers maintain full insurance coverage for their liabilities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: First, I welcome the amendment to commence claims processing upon the Ministry's or the insurer's notification of fatal or serious injuries, thus removing the requirement for employees or their dependants to file compensation claims applications.

sections.label: Compensation for light duties pay
sections.summary: Employers must compensate workers on light duties up to their AME where such duties pay less.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Where such light duties pay less, going forward, employers will need to compensate them up to their AME.

sections.label: Permanent disability benefits and light duties
sections.summary: The speaker suggests pension options and support for permanently disabled workers, and welcomes extending WICA compensation to light duties.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Some cap benefits for permanently disabled workers at 450 weeks while others allow benefits for life or until the worker reaches the age for Social Security benefits.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to suggest that for workers who suffer permanent disabilities, the Ministry consider some form of pension arrangement as an option, as well as regular financial support, perhaps for their children up to the age of 18.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Extending compensation under WICA to include those on light duties due to work injury is a positive change towards covering the potential loss in workers' income because they may not be able to work overtime, given the highly manual and strenuous nature of their work and, hence, losing out on overtime pay or other incentives.

sections.label: MWC cash payments and WICA amendments
sections.summary: NTUC welcomes amendments allowing MOM to order compensation based on salary multiples or AME, and initial CI assessment at six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, in WICA cases assisted by MWC involving many Work Permit holders, especially on the lower end of the skills profile, they continue to be paid in cash without the issuance of any records.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Thus, NTUC welcomes the proposed amendment that allows MOM to order compensation based on a multiple of the worker's basic monthly salary or the AME based on at least 75% of cases of the industry norms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: NTUC also supports the move for initial compensation based on current incapacity (CI) assessment at six months after the work accident to allow for a faster claim resolution for workers.

sections.label: Six-month CI assessment safety net
sections.summary: A safety net provision for CI assessment at six months benefits workers and employers, as WICA covers medical treatment costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As such, having a safety net provision for CI assessment at six months will benefit workers and employers as well because WICA is also meant to cover medical treatment cost for claimants, or at least help to defray the cost of treatment which, for migrant workers, are liable to be borne by employers.

sections.label: Reassessment after six-month CI assessment
sections.summary: The speaker asks what channels exist for workers to seek reassessment if their injury worsens after six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: While the migrant workers will face a shorter waiting time for their claims processing and can return to their home country earlier, I would like to enquire on the channels that would be made available for workers to seek reassessment in the event their injury condition deteriorates after the six-month mark.

sections.label: WICA one-year time bar and ODs
sections.summary: WICA's one-year time bar would exclude occupational diseases with long latency periods, such as asbestosis symptoms appearing after 20 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For example, symptoms of asbestosis may only occur 20 years after exposure but, given WICA’s current one-year time bar, it would exclude such ODs with long latency periods.

sections.label: Insurers process WIC claims
sections.summary: Under the proposed amendments, MOM-licensed insurers will assess and process all WIC claims per MOM guidelines and time standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Under the proposed amendments, MOM-licensed insurers will assess and process all WIC claims as per stipulated MOM guidelines and time standards.

sections.label: Higher compensation limit, more workers
sections.summary: The amendments proposed a higher compensation limit and will include even more workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The amendments proposed a higher compensation limit and will include even more workers.

sections.label: Workplace injury cases in 2018
sections.summary: In 2018, workplace fatal injury cases dropped from the year before, while workplace injury cases rose from 12,498 in 2017 to 12,810.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: In 2018, while there was a drop in the number of workplace fatal injury cases from the year before, workplace injury cases increased from 12,498 cases in 2017 to 12,810 cases in 2018.

sections.label: Doctors referred to SMC
sections.summary: Since 2017, four cases were referred to SMC for investigation where doctors were suspected of issuing inappropriate medical certification to workers with work injuries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Since 2017, there were four cases, referred to SMC for investigation, where doctors were suspected of issuing inappropriate medical certification to workers that had work injuries.

sections.label: Minister of State on insurance
sections.summary: The Minister of State said that 90% of companies are already insured.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Minister of State did say that 90% of companies are already insured.

sections.label: Restitution for false claims
sections.summary: The proposed amendments of the Act will enable restitution to be paid to employers for false claims.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments of the Act will enable restitution to be paid to employers for false claims.

sections.label: Safety protocols and training
sections.summary: Safety protocols and training are the best protection for workers and employers, with employers providing safe environments and employees adhering to safe work practices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Ultimately, the best protection for workers and for employers is to have safety protocols and training to ensure a safe working environment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: While employers have the duty of care to provide a safe working environment for their employees, employees also do need to adhere to safe work practices as they carry out their work, and this will help minimise the number of injuries as well as diseases in the workplace.

sections.label: WICA insurance loading for hazards
sections.summary: Under revised WICA, employers exposing workers to greater occupational hazards pay for those risks through insurance loading.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With the revisions in WICA, employers who expose workers to greater occupational hazards will have to pay for those risks through insurance loading.

sections.label: Incentive for self-employment arrangements
sections.summary: The speaker fears an incentive may be created for employers to promote self-employment arrangements to avoid regulatory costs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Taken together, I fear that we will inadvertently create an incentive for employers to create and promote self-employment arrangements to avoid the regulatory costs.

sections.label: Delivery riders private accident insurance
sections.summary: Josephine Teo noted the WSH Council encouraged food delivery services to provide private accident insurance for self-employed riders, and Deliveroo and GrabFood have done so.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Minister Josephine Teo noted in a reply to a Parliamentary Question earlier this year that the WSH Council has encouraged food delivery services to provide private accident insurance for self-employed riders, and Deliveroo and GrabFood have done so.

sections.label: Insurers assuming employer WICA liabilities
sections.summary: Insurers are essentially assuming the financial liabilities faced by the employer under WICA.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The insurers are essentially assuming the financial liabilities faced by the employer under WICA.

sections.label: Gaps in worker injury protection
sections.summary: A conflict of interest led to a surgeon's conviction, HOME suggested workers choose their medical institution, and self-employed and migrant workers face barriers under WICA.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In one recent case, this conflict of interest resulted in a surgeon being convicted for professional misconduct for providing grossly insufficient post-operative medical leave to a foreign worker.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, HOME has suggested that workers facing a work injury could be granted the right to seek medical treatment and medical reports from a medical institution of their choice.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If so, the costs should be completely claimable from the employer.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The most notable gap now is protection for our self-employed workers and our migrant workers who often face barriers to exercising their rights under WICA.

sections.label: WIC premiums incremental cost
sections.summary: The incremental cost of WIC premiums is 0.015 of the annual total labour cost.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Anyway, the WIC premiums' incremental cost is at 0.015 the annual total labour cost.

sections.label: Foreign workers pay foreign rates
sections.summary: Foreign workers have to pay foreign rates and non-subsidised rates.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: For foreign workers especially, they have to actually pay foreign rates and non-subsidised rates.

sections.label: SMC discipline and MOM guidelines
sections.summary: SMC takes disciplinary action against doctors for non-reporting or insufficient medical leave, and asks if MOM can work with MOH on guidelines and how often it reviews claims and derives the AMF.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: SMC takes serious disciplinary action against doctors for non-reporting or even for insufficient medical leave and assessment which is not done appropriately in relation to injuries.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In this light, perhaps can MOM work with the Ministry of Health (MOH) on a framework or guideline to assist and advise medical practitioners on some kind of algorithmic process, so that there is actually some kind of a loose framework they can refer to?

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Also, how frequently does MOM review the claims compensation amount and how is the AMF derived?

sections.label: Workplace injury cases 2018
sections.summary: In 2018 there were 12,810 workplace injury cases, up from 12,498 in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Last year, 2018 saw 12,810 workplace injury cases, up from 12,498 cases in 2017.

sections.label: Expanding WICA occupational diseases
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked to consider expanding the list of occupational diseases under WICA to include workplace mental health issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry consider expanding the list of occupational diseases covered under WICA to include mental health issues arising from the workplace?

sections.label: Safeguards against insurer exclusion clauses
sections.summary: The question asks what safeguards MOM will put in place to ensure insurers do not diminish insurance coverage adequacy through exclusion clauses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The question is: what are the safeguards that MOM will put in place to ensure that insurers do not diminish the adequacy of such insurance coverage through these exclusion clauses?

sections.label: Workplace accident prevention and WSH training
sections.summary: 41 accident victims died last year, and the speaker proposes mandatory trained WSH representatives and a National WSH Training Academy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, in 41 of the accidents that happened last year, the victims succumbed to their injuries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The prevention of workplace accidents requires a strong company culture geared towards safe workplace practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Therefore, we should make it mandatory for every company to have at least one trained WSH representative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Today, only certain sectors are required to have a WSH officer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Earlier this year, I had proposed to set up a National WSH Training Academy that doubles up as a WSH Centre of Excellence.

sections.label: MOM data analysis for targeted inspections
sections.summary: Analysing claims data from a large sample would let MOM identify lagging sectors and conduct more targeted inspections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: By analysing the data from a large enough sample size of claims, MOM would be able to derive the sectors and subsectors that are lagging in their WSH practices and conduct more targeted inspections.

sections.label: Two triggers in R's case
sections.summary: The passage states that in R's case there were two triggers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: The second point, on R's case, there were two triggers.

sections.label: Why MOM rejected and reviewed case
sections.summary: MOM rejected the case because it was beyond the first year, and on appeal it was reviewed and taken into consideration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: So, that was why it was not picked up, to begin with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: And why MOM rejected in the first place was that it was beyond the first year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Upon appeal, we reviewed it, as I said, and we took it into consideration.

sections.label: Insurers reporting private settlement outcomes
sections.summary: Under the old WICA private settlements were not tracked, but insurers must now report the outcomes of cases they handled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Under the old WICA, we did not track private settlements but, moving forward, as I mentioned in my speech earlier, insurers have to report back on the outcomes of the cases that they handled.

sections.label: Timebar, new laws and insurance coverage
sections.summary: The case breached the one-year timebar, but new laws will accept such claims more readily and MOM will define core insurance terms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: You already breached the one-year timebar and, therefore, the case is not admissible by current laws.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: But moving forward, under the new laws, we will be able to accept these claims a lot more readily and, therefore, make the appeals clearer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: MOM will define a core set of insurance terms and conditions to prevent unfair exclusion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: Since we are encouraging older workers to remain employable, will MOM ensure that the insurance companies will provide coverage for all workers, regardless of age, as long as they are manual or non-manual employees earning up to $2,600?

sections.label: Mental illness work injury claims
sections.summary: A Member says they are delighted the Minister of State confirms workers are entitled to claims for mental illness resulting from work injury or at work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: The second clarification – I am absolutely delighted that the Minister of State is confirming that workers are entitled to claims for mental illness resulting from work injury or at work.

sections.label: Mental illness accident link, insurer licensing
sections.summary: The Minister stresses mental illness must be linked to an accident, such as PTSD diagnosed by a doctor, and notes insurers are licensed under the new WICA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: I would answer the second question first, on mental illness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: I have to stress again that it has to be linked to an accident.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: In an accident case where you have PTSD, for example, that will be something we could cover but you have to show that cause, diagnosed by a doctor, to show that link to an accident.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: As for insurers, the one thing that is different with the new WICA and the old WICA is that we are licensing the insurers.

sections.label: PTSD cases cited
sections.summary: The speaker cites PTSD as an example and says three cases were done, all PTSD-related.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: As I have mentioned earlier, one example is PTSD.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: So, we have done three and all three were PTSD-related.
